The beach at the Isle of Pines de magnificent, clean, firmly packed white
sand gently sloping towerd and into a land looked lagoon where the water is clear
is orystal. We are in one of ter native huts with heavily thatched roof and met
sides but nard wood floors, electric lights and tiled bath. Very attractive and
right on the beaon. Ite unkind to write this but we are having the kind of
weather I like- when you are nevor cold. Everyone dresses sensibly. I suppose
we men are indebted to Douglas NacArtour for the open neck-no necktie style.
Praotically no one wears a coat. The Grand Pacifio Hotel in Suva suggested that
men were expected to wear ties at dinner but no coats and most men wear short
sleeved shirts. The only ones who do not dress appropiately for the hot olimate
are the natives. before the missionaries came they wore nothing or practically
nothing..Now, tee women wear two garments, one wrapped around them ull length with
amother over-riding dress to just below their knees.

Deo. 14th, This Ile Des Fins (Pine Tree Island) was claimed by the French in
1853 and shortly afterward they made it into a prison. If the prisoners were
permitted on the besen they probably never bad it so good. The temperature ranges
from 60 to 80 all year round. I should think it would have led to an increase in
crime such as occured in the little town of lake george when a well intentioned
lady do-gooder was shooked at the appearance and life in the local clink.
She
provided beauty reat mattresses, ankle deep rugs, chintz curtains and eleotric
- blankets. 4 special chef provided steaks, roast beef, eto., Never has there been
such a percenta ge increase in crime. Bums came from miles around to shy a brick
through a window and then stand around tobe arrested and serve a six months
sentence. They could get another six months by telling the judge they hoped when he
got home his mother would come out from under the porch and bite him. It must
bave been something like that in France except that the condemned night be sent to
Devil's Island inatead of here. Debby and I have found 20 different kinds of
shells on the beach here.
Saturday afternoon, Deo, 14th/ Debby and I have just returned from an ex-
parience which could only take place in Prench territory. Yesterday there were
only a few people here but today around lunch time they started moving in from
every direction. Debby had been talking alot with a young Frenchman who has beeh
divine Tor shells and aas at least one quite valuable one. We had been talking to
him about a trip out to a reef where we might find some better shells. He suggested
et lunch time that we go out at 2:30 so at that time Deb and I went down in front
of the Gentral eating plage where he keeps the boat and got in expecting him to
taice oft right away. The boat is about the size of Joe Barker's, perhaps 15 feet
long with 2.45 i.P. Evinrude outboard engines. After Debby and I waited for the
Prenohman to leave and he cept looking shoreward expectantly, a very dizzy brunette
got in and then a bus load of people arrived and started boarding our boat like
alot of pirates. when they all got in, believe it or not, we counted 18 grown ups
and 9 children. If there was a life preserver on board it was not in evidence. The
sKipper could not look ahead because of the congestion on the front deck so he
stood on the gunnel to spot the reefs, and there were pleaty of them, reaching in
to steer the boat now and then. We went quite a long way to a small island where
everybody went ashore in two feet of water.
